subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Final Fantasy-style gunblade prop, around 1.4 meters long, modeled as a static piece without joints since it doesn't need articulation. I'm thinking through how to orient it so it stands upright with its lowest point touching the floor at y=0.

I'm sketching out the overall layout along the Y axis: a lathed pommel at the base, a wrapped leather grip with a trigger guard, and deciding which way the blade's flat faces and cutting edge should orient so the gun mechanism and spine read clearly to a viewer looking along +Z.

For the guard loop, I'll use a swept closed path rather than extrusion since I need a ring shape with an opening, with the trigger as a small separate extrusion inside it. Then for the blade, I'm extruding an outline from the base near the guard up to the tip, tapering the width and thickness toward a pointed, angled tip.

I want to simplify the thickness to a constant value, and add a separate thicker extrusion to represent the spine/barrel bar running partway up the blade. Rather than modeling a true edge bevel with separate plates, I'll fake the brightness gradient near the cutting edge using a paint function based on the x-coordinate.

I'm also planning additional textures to sell the Squall gunblade look: a lion emblem on the guard/pommel, rune engravings glowing cyan on the blade, and chamber/barrel details on the cylinder face near the tip.

I'm thinking about adding a small dangling chain with a lion-ring pendant off the pommel, kept above y=0, using a few torus links along a simple path. Then I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and parts with flat colors, noting there are no joints needed since this is a static model, and starting to lay out the component palette.

Now I'm defining the color palette using steel and gilt metal paints from the clockwork kit, plus dark, leather, and blue accent tones, then plotting the sword's coordinates starting with a lathed pommel profile in gilt with a small ring collar, followed by the cylindrical grip section.

For the grip, I'm adding octagonal leather-grain sides and a few thin dark rings as wrap bands, then placing a gilt ferrule block to mount the guard. I'm also working out a revolver-style cylinder housing near the base of the blade, with chamber and emblem textures mapped onto its front and back circular faces, set against a dark steel body.

Now I'm sketching the hammer at the rear top of the cylinder, then working out the blade root and crossguard outlines, adjusting coordinates so the gilt wing-shaped guard flares properly without overlapping the cylinder geometry.

Still writing blade outline coordinates...

Still shaping the barrel and spine geometry...

Defining edge paint logic...

Now I'm sketching the trigger guard geometry as a closed curved path around the grip area, connecting points near the ferrule down along one side.

I'm adding a hex gilt cylinder for the ferrule, then designing a hanging chain pendant off the guard with torus-ring links and a stylized lion-head medallion built from simple SVG shapes.

For the texture, I'm placing amber holes in a gold ring with a center blue gem, considering whether to make it glow, then shaping the hammer as an extruded dark outline hooking back from the grip, and weighing whether to add bandolier cartridge details or a blue ribbon accent.

I'm adding a blue cloth wrap on the lower grip, considering gilt wing or lion emblem plates on the ricasso using decal planes instead of extruded shapes, and deciding to skip extra pommel gem or ring details. I'm checking that the floor placement works with the pommel at y=0 and the chain hanging above it, with the blade standing vertical and untilted.

Now I'm writing helper functions for part placement and planes for decals, handling orientation and axis direction, then adding a glow effect to textured parts. I'm defining SVG textures for runes and a lion emblem, generating glyph paths for the runes and procedurally building mane spikes, face, eyes, and nose for the lion design.

Writing cylinder and lathe pommel geometry...

For the chain, I'm placing torus links along the polyline path using frame orientation so each ring follows the tangent direction, alternating rotation between adjacent links for a realistic interlocking look.

Now I'm working out the hanging chain path from the crossguard wing tip down to the lower point, and refining the wing outline coordinates to position where the chain attaches.

Chain and pendant placement...

For blade metal, I'll mix steel tones and use the paint, mix, noise, and smoothstep utilities from the SDK to build the material functions.
